newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off on indecision, thin volume. [CORRECTED 21:34 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off on indecision, thin volume. [CORRECTED 21:34 GMT]

text.p: Mexican stocks closed down on Monday due to caution ahead of third-quarter earnings reports but did rebound from support, traders said.

"We see indecision ahead of earnings reports. The Street's enthusiasm was dampened by lower-than-expected retail sales figures on Friday," said Ramon Ruiz, sales trader at the Bankers Trust Latin American equity desk.
The blue chip IPC lost 33.60 points (corrects from "the blue chip IPC gained 33.60 points"), or 1.01 percent, to 3,286.04. Volume was low at 61.8 million shares.
"When volume is this thin, however, I don't give much credence to market directions," Ruiz added.
Ruiz said caution also was due to concerns that inflation, particularly in energy costs, would eat into margins for industrial companies.

Local traders meanwhile confirmed that cement stocks were hit hard during the session on expectations that results would be less than favorable. Market heavyweight Cemex CPO shares, for example, ended down 70 centavos at 27.60 pesos.

One blue chip that withstood the slide was media group Televisa, up two pesos to 110.00 pesos. Traders said this was in response to a statement by Unilever that it may assign some of its hefty advertising budget to Televisa in the future.
Traders also noted that financial stocks were mixed. GFB, for example, was sold ahead of an expected unfavorable report, while Banacci was in demand.
The prospect of primary rate hikes also slowed down trade and depressed share prices, traders said.
"We're expecting primary (Cetes) hikes of 100 to 200 basis points to shore up the peso, which doesn't particularly help equities at an uncertain time," one trader said.
Traders also noted that although the IPC slid, it did rebound at a support level of 3,274 points in the closing minutes of trade.
